question: Which cloud provider's managed object storage and on-upload malware scanning will Unbound use for inbound artifacts?
recommendation: Choose a provider with native on-upload object scanning (AWS GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 or Microsoft Defender for Storage); if GCP is chosen for other reasons, budget a licensed scanning engine inside the platform network.
alternatives: AWS (GuardDuty S3, $0.09/GB + $0.215/1,000 objects);Azure (Defender for Storage, $0.15/GB + ~$9.78/account-month);GCP (no native scanner; ClamAV ~60% commodity detection or licensed engine);Note: S3 presigned uploads can bind a SHA-256 checksum; Azure SAS cannot, so Azure needs server-side hash verification on commit (review R2-23)
rationale: Malware inspection must not be custom-built; only AWS and Azure offer native on-upload scanning with fail-closed primitives (FIE-C-001..012). The cloud choice is broader than ingestion, so it is the owner's.

question: May inbound artifact bytes live in managed object storage as a non-authoritative, content-addressed store referenced from PostgreSQL (ADR-ING-002), given CNV-ARC-001's restriction on a second durable store?
recommendation: Approve ADR-ING-002: bytes in object storage (non-authoritative, write-once, hash-referenced), every fact, state and queue entry in PostgreSQL.
alternatives: All bytes in PostgreSQL bytea (1 GB value limit, ~10x storage cost with HA, backup/WAL growth, no native scanner, no WORM);Hybrid threshold (two code paths)
rationale: CNV-ARC-001 allows a second store only if objectives cannot otherwise be met; native malware scanning, write-once retention and legal hold exist only on object storage (FIE-C-027..030), and keeping file bytes out of WAL keeps PostgreSQL RTO/RPO achievable.

question: Which formats will the launch sponsor's bank deliver for prior-day reporting, lockbox and ACH returns (BAI2 or camt.053; lockbox layout; NACHA return files or bank reporting)?
recommendation: Build the canonical bank-transaction model once and implement exactly one bank's adapter in release 1 (CNV-PAY-007); obtain the bank's implementation guides and sample files under contract before building.
alternatives: Implement BAI2 and camt.053 speculatively (wasted work if the bank uses one);Bank API only
rationale: Bank layouts are contract-only (FIE-B-035, CNV-EVB-001) and there is no design partner (OD-M-14); this is an activation gate, not a product decision.

question: Which AI document-processing path is approved first, and is AI extraction enabled by default for sponsors?
decision_owner: Product owner with security and privacy
recommendation: Off by default; first approve the chosen cloud's document-AI service (OCR and prebuilt check/bank-statement models at ~$1.50-$10 per 1,000 pages) running in-region; allow LLM-based proposals (via the same cloud's model hosting with no data retention) only for appraisals, death certificates and determination letters after their evaluation sets pass.
alternatives: Third-party LLM API with zero-data-retention agreement;No AI extraction in release 1
rationale: AI improves review speed for unstructured evidence but no public accuracy benchmark exists for DAF documents (FIE-C-048); disclosure terms are a privacy decision (CNV-GOV-010).

question: What retention applies to security-rejected bytes and to unreleased quarantine objects?
decision_owner: Sponsor compliance owner with security owner
recommendation: Security-rejected and malware-positive bytes: 1 year (metadata and verdict 10 years); quarantine objects expire 7 days after release or rejection; abandoned partial uploads deleted at slot expiry.
alternatives: Keep rejected bytes 10 years (stores live malware long-term);Delete immediately (loses incident evidence)
rationale: Rejected bytes are security evidence, not financial records; CNV-PLT-004's 10-year floor applies to transaction evidence and is kept for metadata.

question: Should release 1 operate an Unbound-hosted inbound SFTP endpoint?
recommendation: No. Pull from partner-hosted SFTP or APIs; add a managed inbound SFTP service only when a contracted partner can only push.
alternatives: Managed inbound SFTP from day one (fixed monthly cost per endpoint, key management, another surface)
rationale: Banks and custodians publish files on their own SFTP/download services and APIs (FIE-B-055..057, FIE-B-060); a pull client needs no inbound infrastructure.

question: Is email an ingestion channel in release 1?
recommendation: No. Email is not authority-bearing; auto-replies direct senders to the portal. Revisit only for classification of correspondence into cases.
alternatives: Authorized-sender email ingestion with DMARC checks
rationale: Business email compromise losses ($2.77B in 2024, FIE-B-019) and low DMARC enforcement (17.6% p=reject, FIE-B-020) make email unsuitable for instructions.

question: Is XLSX accepted for financial imports?
recommendation: No: CSV templates for financial imports; XLSX only for migration and onboarding configuration, values only.
rationale: XLSX adds a ZIP container, formulas and external links for no data benefit over CSV; spreadsheet tools export CSV.

question: Are per-tenant encryption keys used for artifacts at launch?
recommendation: Per-environment provider-managed keys at launch with tenant-prefix access policies; per-tenant keys enabled per sponsor contract (crypto-erasure on exit) without data migration.
alternatives: Per-tenant keys for all sponsors from day one (key-count cost, operational burden)
rationale: Tenant isolation is enforced by prefix policies plus application authorization; per-tenant keys add value mainly for contractual exit assurance.

question: How are ingestion costs priced: inside a ~20 bps servicing fee, or with separate fees for migration and new-institution onboarding?
recommendation: Absorb routine ingestion (bank, custodian, IRS/OFAC, bulk grants, evidence documents) in the servicing fee only on shared multi-tenant infrastructure; charge sponsor migration and onboarding of an institution with no existing mapping as fixed fees; set a per-fund minimum fee for small-balance books.
rationale: Under assumed handling times (daf-landscape fie_economics.py v2, revised after adversarial review R3), routine ingestion takes about 8% of 20 bps revenue for a $150k book at 90% routine STP (about 6% with prevention), about 23% for a $50k book, about 19% pooled and 45% standalone at 1,000 funds, and more than the whole fee if investigations run at 3-5% x 135 minutes. Onboarding and migration are lumpy fixed costs small sponsors cannot amortise. Ingestion cost is a slice of, not an addition to, total operating cost.

question: How often are released documents re-scanned?
recommendation: On every security-policy version change for the format, and every 30 days for documents attached to open cases; closed-case documents are re-scanned before any re-distribution.
alternatives: Re-scan everything nightly (cost grows with retained volume);Never re-scan
rationale: Scanning costs about $0.09-$0.15 per GB (FIE-C-001, FIE-C-006); open-case documents are the ones people still open.

question: Is a digital mailroom vendor part of release 1?
recommendation: Conditional: only for a launch sponsor with material paper mail; integrate the vendor's PDF + index delivery through an evidence profile.
rationale: Paper and fax remain first-class channels at the largest sponsors (FIE-A-134) but volume depends on the sponsor; vendors price around $2 per envelope (FIE-B-061).

question: Which isolation primitive runs the inspector role?
recommendation: The chosen cloud's container job or function sandbox in a subnet with no outbound route except storage and database private endpoints, deployed from the same binary with an inspector role flag.
alternatives: Separate inspection service codebase (violates component monolith);In-process parsing (no isolation)
rationale: Parser CVEs (FIE-C-033..035) justify isolation; a role flag keeps one codebase (Conditor role-flag precedent).

question: May sponsor administrators author new ingestion profiles themselves?
recommendation: No. Sponsors tune only the bounded sponsor_configurable attributes; new profiles and mappings are platform versions reviewed by engineering (AI-assisted), keeping the catalog closed.
alternatives: Self-service profile workbench with mapping editor
rationale: An open mapping editor becomes an uncontrolled programming environment and multiplies support (mission §10, §22).
